body:
### Summary

uv aborted while synchronizing dependencies when stderr was redirected to a file on a quota-exhausted filesystem.

The underlying storage failure was caused by my execution environment. I’m reporting the subsequent `SIGABRT` to ask whether uv should exit with a controlled error when writing a diagnostic fails.

The original sequence was:

```bash
uv sync --frozen --group dev --python 3.12 --quiet;
uv run --frozen --group dev pytest ... \
  > /tmp/tests.log 2>&1
```

Both the virtual environment and the log were located on `/tmp`, a tmpfs with a per-user quota. The first command failed to copy a dependency with `Disk quota exceeded`. Because I used `;`, the second command still ran and attempted synchronization again.

The core dump places the panic in `uv_fs::link::atomic_hardlink_overwrite`, at the hardlink fallback warning. Inspection of the saved error identifies a failed stderr write with `EDQUOT`.

#### Reproduction

I reduced this to a synthetic wheel containing one Python module:

1. Put the uv cache and installation target on different filesystems.
2. Create the module’s destination file beforehand to exercise atomic replacement.
3. Install with `--link-mode=hardlink`.
4. Inject `EDQUOT` into stderr writes containing the warning.

Without injection, uv prints the hardlink warning, copies the file, and succeeds. With injection:

```text
thread 'main2' panicked at crates/uv-fs/src/link.rs:812:9:
failed printing to stderr: Disk quota exceeded (os error 122)
```

The subprocess exits with `-6` (`SIGABRT`).

This reproduces with Fedora’s 0.12.19 package, Astral’s official 0.12.19 binary, and Astral’s official 0.12.23 binary.

The injected error reproduces the crash mechanism; the original incident involved an actual filesystem quota failure.

#### Expected behavior / policy question

Would a controlled nonzero exit be preferable to a panic and core dump when diagnostic output fails with a permanent error such as `EDQUOT`?

I’m not proposing retries or assuming installation should continue after storage exhaustion. I’m also aware of #22170 and the discussion in #22195 about unsupported nonblocking stdio. This case involves a regular redirected log file and a permanent quota error rather than `EAGAIN`.

If this behavior is considered worth changing, I’d be interested in contributing a focused regression test and discussing the appropriate error-handling policy before implementing it.

### Platform

Fedora Linux 44, x86_64

### Version

uv 0.12.19 (Fedora: 0.12.19-1.fc44); also reproduced on official uv 0.12.23 - both x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu

### Python version

Python 3.12.14
title: uv aborts when a hardlink fallback warning cannot be written to stderr (EDQUOT)
